title: Codec Latent-Space Map
description: A per-model dialect for the Codec binary transport protocol's latent modalities (image-latents, video-latents, v0.3+). Describes the latent tensor shape and dtype, references one or more runtime-portable decoder graphs (ONNX / ggml / safetensors / WGSL) by content-addressed hash, lists the transform pipelines (raw / int8 / delta+int8 / ...) the latents may travel under, and optionally declares pre-trained zstd dictionaries for each (format, pipeline) pair. Maps are content-addressed and immutable — a new model version or decoder export publishes a new map at a new URL with a new sha256 hash.

id.description: Stable, globally unique latent-space identifier (convention: lowercase 'org/model-name', e.g. 'stabilityai/sd-vae-ft-mse'). Same ID + same hash means byte-identical map. Lives in the latent-space namespace, separate from tokenizer-map IDs.

version.description: Schema version. '1' for the current schema. Bumped only on backward-incompatible changes; additive fields land in additive point releases (1.1, 1.2, ...) without changing the major version.

space_kind.description:
What kind of learned compression produces latents in this space:
  vae — variational autoencoder (continuous latent, a paired decoder reconstructs pixels). Covers Stable Diffusion VAEs, SDXL VAE, video-model VAEs.

Future kinds (audio-codec discrete tokens, neural-network-trained image codecs) will be added additively; clients MUST reject space_kind values they do not understand rather than silently treating them as 'vae'.

shape.description: Per-frame latent tensor shape, **excluding** the batch dimension. For SD-1 at 512×512 this is [4, 64, 64] (channels, height, width). For video models the shape is also per-frame; a video stream emits one LatentFrame per shape-sized tensor.

dtype.description: Element dtype of the **raw** latent — the dtype the model produces before any pipeline transform. This is the dtype seen under pipeline='raw'. Pipelines like 'int8' convert at the wire boundary; the canonical map dtype stays the model's native dtype.

vae_scale_factor.description: The model's known latent scale factor (e.g. 0.18215 for SD-1 / SD-2, 0.13025 for SDXL). Decoders multiply latents by this scale before the first conv block. Carrying it in the map lets clients build a complete decode pipeline from the map alone, without re-deriving the constant per model.

decoders.description: One or more runtime-portable decoder graph references. A client picks the entry whose 'runtime' it can execute (advertised in 'accept_decoders' at HELLO). Multiple entries let a single latent-space map serve clients across runtimes from one CDN pin. All entries MUST decode the same latent space — i.e. plug-compatible at the latent boundary.

runtime.description:
Decoder runtime:
  onnx-web      — ONNX Runtime Web (browser, WebGPU/WebGL/wasm).
  onnx          — ONNX Runtime native (Python / .NET / Java / Rust 'ort' crate).
  torch         — torch + diffusers checkpoint, loaded by the Python client.
  ggml          — ggml/gguf weights, used by libcodec via stable-diffusion.cpp.
  wgsl          — WebGPU compute shader bundle for browsers without ONNX-Web.
  safetensors-pt — raw .safetensors with a torch architecture descriptor.

url.description: Absolute HTTPS URL of the decoder graph bytes. MAY be on any HTTPS origin (the maintainer's own, jsDelivr, R2, Hugging Face, etc.).

hash.description: sha256 digest of the decoder bytes at 'url'. Format 'sha256:<hex>'. The bytes are content-addressed; clients MUST verify the hash before loading the decoder, and SHOULD cache by hash indefinitely.

size_bytes.description: Decoder size in bytes. Carried in the map so clients can budget bandwidth + memory before fetching.

input_shape.description: Decoder graph input shape including the batch dimension, e.g. [1, 4, 64, 64]. Per-batch-1 inference is the canonical form; servers that batch internally still emit per-frame latents.

input_dtype.description: Element dtype the decoder graph expects at its input. May differ from the latent-space 'dtype' (e.g. an int8 pipeline dequantizes to fp16 before the decoder).

output.description: What the decoder produces. Carried in the map so clients can wire the post-decode pipeline (e.g. tone-mapping, BGR→RGB swap) without runtime probing.

format.description: Pixel format of the decoder output. rgb_uint8 is the common case (HWC, 0–255). yuv420p_uint8 is video-decoder-style and skips the chroma upsample step on the GPU side.

shape.description: Output tensor shape including batch dim, e.g. [1, 3, 512, 512] for CHW or [1, 512, 512, 3] for HWC. The 'format' field disambiguates channel order.

license.description: SPDX license identifier (or 'proprietary'). VAE checkpoint licenses vary; carrying the license in the map lets enterprise clients gate the fetch.

pipelines.description: Names of the transform pipelines this map supports on the wire. Each entry MUST appear in the normative pipeline registry defined by spec/PIPELINES.md. 'raw' is mandatory for every map and is the negotiation fallback — when client and server share no other pipeline, they MUST land on 'raw'. The server picks one of these at HELLO/READY based on the client's 'accept_pipelines' list. Adding a non-registry pipeline is a protocol violation; pipelines are not extensible per-deployment.

zstd_dictionaries.description: Pre-trained zstd dictionaries for transport compression. Each entry is keyed by (format, pipeline) — the two axes that define the byte distribution the dict is trained against. A dict trained for one (format, pipeline) pair is meaningless against any other pair; servers MUST NOT respond with Content-Encoding: zstd unless they have loaded a dict whose (format, pipeline) matches the response.

format.description: Codec wire format the dict is trained against.

pipeline.description: Pipeline the dict is trained against. MUST be one of the pipelines listed in the parent 'pipelines' array.

video.description: Optional video-modality metadata. Present only on latent-space maps backed by video models. Image-only VAEs omit this block.

default_fps.description: Default frame rate for streams from this latent-space when the request doesn't specify one.

keyframe_interval.description: Recommended distance between keyframes in delta-coded pipelines. Smaller = more keyframes = bigger wire, faster client recovery from packet loss.

temporal_axis.description:
per-frame  — one LatentFrame per output frame (most VAEs).
block      — the latent encodes a fixed block of frames (e.g. some video-LDM variants); LatentFrame carries the whole block, decoder unrolls.

published_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp. Telemetry only — clients ignore it.
